summary: Hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings and reranking flow for improving search relevance. Demonstrated Redwood embeddings endpoint, how to index vectors, and the reranker endpoint that takes candidates and returns scored order. Discussed latency, cost tradeoffs, and enterprise security (SOC 2/KMS/VPC). Agreed to run a 2-week pilot using BlueCove sample logs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-14 16:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Leo (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Priya (Head of Search), Ethan (Backend), Sofia (Data Scientist), Mike (CTO)

[00:00] Maya: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood Inference, i'll hand off to Leo for the technical walkthrough in a sec but quick agenda — embeddings demo, how customers typically do candidate generation + reranking, then live console + example requests, and finally next steps for a pilot

[00:18] Priya: hi thanks, excited. quick context — we're redoing site search across 35M SKUs, currently using Elastic with keyword + BM25, and then a simple ML rerank that's pretty slow to update. main asks are: better recall for long tail queries, faster iteration for merch tweaks, and tighter latency of p95 under 200ms

[00:40] Leo: great, thanks Priya. i'll start with the hosted API flow — two parts: embedding generation and reranker. embeddings endpoint returns a vector (we demo 768-d and 1536-d options depending on model). you can store vectors in your vector DB or use Redwood's integrated indexing helper for quick POCs.

[01:05] Ethan: when you say integrated indexing helper, is that a hosted index or just a client library?

[01:12] Leo: it's client-side helper + optional hosted index service. for production most folks pair Redwood embeddings with Pinecone or a managed vector DB, but we also have quick hosted indexes for pilots — note, for enterprise deployments we recommend Dedicated or Private for data residency

[01:30] Jordan: i'll share my screen for a quick console demo. (screen share) here is the Redwood Console, model catalog on the left — we're selecting the embeddings model, you can tune parameters like dim, normalize, and quantization profile. then the test panel to run a sample text -> vector call.

[02:05] Sofia: are your embeddings normalized by default? we rely on cosine similarity for reranking currently.

[02:12] Leo: default depends on model; we expose both raw and normalized vectors. for cosine you can either normalize client-side or request normalized output — small note: normalization affects downstream distance computation and latency slightly because some indexes prefer dot product on normalized vectors which is equivalent to cosine

[02:35] Mike: curious about tokenization and costs — what's the unit cost? per-embedding?

[02:42] Maya: hosted pricing is per-embedding call; we'll send targeted estimates but as a rough number, 768-d embeddings on hosted API come in lower unit cost; plus there's a per-request compute component for reranker calls. we'll include sample math for your 1M queries/month in the follow-up

[03:05] Leo: switching to reranker — the endpoint accepts a query plus a list of candidates (text or ids with metadata). it returns a re-scored list with scores and optional explanations. it's meant to be an add-on step after your candidate retrieval. the benefit is you can use a high-precision cross-encoder style model without re-encoding whole corpus.

[03:40] Priya: so we still need a vector DB for candidate retrieval?

[03:45] Leo: yes typical pipeline: 1) embeddings for documents -> index, 2) ANN search returns top-K candidates, 3) reranker endpoint takes query+K and returns ranked output. you can also hybrid with BM25 hits to increase recall.

[04:10] Ethan: how large can K be before reranker latency blows up?

[04:15] Leo: good q. we've optimized the reranker for up to K=50 in hosted low-latency config. p95 depends on sequence lengths — typically 50 candidates with average 50 tokens each gives p95 ~ 180-250ms on hosted depending on model size. Dedicated can push that down. you can also set a timeout and fallback to a cheap scoring if exceeded.

[04:45] Sofia: any support for custom features in the reranker, like price or recency signals?

[04:50] Jordan: yes the reranker accepts structured metadata fields per candidate; you can include numeric features and we can include them in the final scoring function or use them as constraints. many customers pass in category, price delta, inventory flags.

[05:10] Maya: quick demo — we'll run an end-to-end sample: take a query "waterproof hiking jacket for winter" pull candidates from a baseline retrieval, then call the reranker.

[05:22] (sound of typing)

[05:30] [08:00] Jordan: ok sending the POST to /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-768, body: {"input":"waterproof hiking jacket for winter"} getting vector back: [0.001, -0.22, ...] (truncated). indexing tip: store as float16 if your vector DB supports it to save space.

[08:30] Priya: we have strict PCI-adjacent workloads; any data touched by embeddings stays encrypted?

[08:36] Leo: yes hosted API encrypts data at rest and in transit, and we support KMS integration for Dedicated/Private. for PCI-level constraints we usually recommend Private deployment. we'll include SOC2 and encryption docs. small caveat: hosted pilot traces may have ephemeral logs for debugging unless you opt out.

[09:00] Ethan: what's the retention of logs and raw payloads?

[09:05] Maya: by default logs retained 30 days in hosted; Dedicated/Private you control retention. we'll send the arch doc with retention and deletion policies.

[09:30] [12:00] Jordan: now calling the reranker endpoint with topK ids and original texts. (request) got response — reranked top 5 with scores: 0.92, 0.87, 0.78, ... and optional justification tokens flagged.

[12:30] Sofia: nice, can you show how we would A/B test models?

[12:36] Leo: Console supports rollouts: you can create two reranker model routes and do canary splits or percentage-based traffic. also Redwood Optimize will suggest batching and quant profiles to reduce cost without hurting relevance based on your eval set.

[13:10] Priya: how do we validate that reranker doesn't hallucinate or change SKU ids? we can't have mismatched product ids in results

[13:18] Leo: we never rewrite IDs; the reranker returns the candidate id you provided plus a score. it may provide a textual explanation but we treat that as metadata. there's also a strict mode that only reorders input candidates and disallows any synthetic additions.

[13:45] Mike: performancewise, do we need KV cache for reranker?

[13:52] Leo: KV cache is more relevant to autoregressive generation. for reranker which is essentially cross-encoding, caching helps if you have repeated query patterns and same candidates — Redwood supports prefix caching and results-level caching at the route layer. that can reduce p95 significantly for repeat queries.

[14:30] Ethan: can we run the reranker against late-binding product metadata that changes frequently? e.g., prices update every hour

[14:40] Jordan: yes pass in the live metadata in the candidate payload; we don't require re-indexing to reflect price changes for reranking decisions.

[15:10] Sofia: i'd like to run offline evals — what do you need?

[15:16] Leo: an anonymized sample of query logs and the ground-truth clicks or conversions is ideal. we'll run baseline embeddings+ANN + reranker and return precision@k, NDCG, and latency/cost estimates. Priya if you can share a ~10k query sample we'll run a quick bench.

[15:32] Priya: ok we'll prepare that, anonymized and remove PII.

[15:40] Maya: quick note on model choices — for reranker we use a small cross-encoder for latency-sensitive paths and larger models for quality-sensitive paths; Redwood Optimize will recommend which to choose given your eval set and cost target.

[16:00] (background: brief interruption as someone joins late)

[16:10] Mike: what's your approach to multi-language support? we have EU/UK + Spanish sites

[16:16] Leo: model catalog includes multilingual embedding models; we also support locale-aware reranker configurations. if you want language-specific recall we recommend language-specific embedding indices and then a reranker model trained/finetuned on the target language — we can discuss fine-tuning options in the pilot.

[16:40] Ethan: any throttling or rate limits we should be aware of?

[16:45] Maya: hosted has default rate limits per account, we can raise them for pilots. Dedicated gives you dedicated throughput and predictable p95; we can sketch capacity numbers for your traffic profile.

[17:05] Sofia: about vector dimensionality — do you support quantized 128-d alternatives?

[17:12] Leo: we have model variants and quantization profiles — 128-d is possible with distilled embeddings but may reduce recall on long-tail; Optimize will suggest quant/dim tradeoffs after seeing your data.

[17:40] Priya: security again — SAML/SSO for console access?

[17:46] Jordan: yes SSO with SAML/OIDC, RBAC at the route and token level, audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM for Private/Dedicated.

[18:10] Maya: ok let's recap action items and next steps.

[18:18] Maya: next steps: we'll send the code snippets and a step-by-step for the end-to-end pipeline, plus a cost estimate. Leo will run a quick eval on your sample logs once you provide them, and we'll schedule a pilot kickoff for next week.

[18:35] Priya: that sounds good. one ask — can you include a sample of the reranker request/response schema so our infra can wire it up?

[18:42] Jordan: yes we'll include request/response examples and a small js/python client snippet.

[18:55] Ethan: what's a realistic SLA for p95 on hosted? you mentioned 180-250ms but that's optimistic

[19:00] Leo: correct, that's for small model reranker and depends on sequence length and K. for conservative planning assume 300ms p95 on hosted for K=50; Dedicated can drop to ~120-180ms depending on GPU and model variant. we'll include a latency SLO table.

[19:25] Mike: do you have references from other ecommerce customers?

[19:30] Maya: yes we'll share two anonymized case studies and a customer contact if you want direct reference.

[19:40] Priya: ok final question — any pitfalls you commonly see when integrating?

[19:46] Leo: common ones: 1) not normalizing embeddings consistently between index and query, 2) choosing K too small and missing recall, 3) forgetting to include business features in reranker input. we provide a checklist in the integration guide.

[20:10] (wrap up)

[20:15] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials in one email. thanks Priya and team for your time.

[20:30] Priya: thanks all.

End transcript.
